gloss: to fish up; to hike up (prices)

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {釣|つ}り{上|あ}げませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {釣|つ}り{上|あ}げていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {釣|つ}り{上|あ}げていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to fish up; to reel in; to catch and pull up
definitions.explanation: To pull a fish out of the water. Can also refer to lifting something up with a hook or line.

definitions.gloss: to raise; to hike up (prices, wages)
definitions.explanation: To artificially or forcefully raise prices, wages, or other values, often with a negative connotation of manipulation.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{魚|さかな}を{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: I reeled in a big fish.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{見事|みごと}に{鯛|たい}を{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: My father splendidly reeled in a sea bream.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{初|はじ}めて{自分|じぶん}で{魚|さかな}を{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げて、とても{喜|よろこ}んでいた。
examples.english: The child was very happy to reel in a fish by themselves for the first time.

examples.japanese: {物価|ぶっか}を{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げる。
{転売|てんばい}{業者|ぎょうしゃ}が{値段|ねだん}を{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げている。
examples.english: Resellers are driving up the prices.

examples.japanese: {需要|じゅよう}が{高|たか}まると、{価格|かかく}が{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げられることがある。
examples.english: When demand rises, prices can sometimes be hiked up.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 is literal fishing. Sense 2 is figurative and carries a negative connotation of price manipulation or artificial inflation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魚|さかな}を{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げる (to reel in a fish)
- {値段|ねだん}を{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げる (to hike up prices)
- {物価|ぶっか}を{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げる (to drive up commodity prices)
- {目|め}を{釣|つ}り{上|あ}げる (to narrow one's eyes in anger — a separate idiomatic use)
